Exploring Enablers of Sustainable Ecotourism through Actor-Network Theory and Social Network Analysis

Abstract:

Ecotourism and community are two inseparable terms. Networks among the stakeholders in tourism are studied through several network studies such as stakeholder theory, social network analysis, actor network theory etc. in ecotourism studies local community and its involvement in management, training, awareness are important components. This study employs Actor-Network Theory (ANT) to analyse the interrelationships among human and non-human elements that enable sustainable ecotourism development. It identifies and categorise enablers of ecotourism&mdashsuch as government programs, infrastructure, education, digital platforms, and community participation&mdashinto human actors, non-human actors, and actants. Applying ANT offers a holistic understanding of the socio-ecological networks that constitute ecotourism, enabling more integrated planning and management approaches. Social network analysis (SNA) is applied to find the social capital and its type between the community organisation working at the ecotourism site. This framework helps identify leverage points for enhancing collaboration, improving governance, and promoting community-based, environmentally responsible tourism practices.
